draft.title: Deciding with criteria
card: Criteria are the things that matter when you choose, such as cost, risk and fairness. Choose them before you look at the options.
Score each option against each criterion, for example from 1 (poor) to 5 (very good).
Add up the scores for each option. The option with the best total does best overall.
If one criterion matters more, it can be given extra weight. Then the best option may change.
draft.remember: Set criteria, score every option against them, then pick the best overall.

a.q: A school club must choose a fundraiser. It scores three options from 1 to 5 on cost, risk and fairness. Which option should it choose?
opts: The one with the highest total score
The one with the lowest cost only
The one most members chose first
The one with the highest single score
a.why: The method is to score every option against every criterion and pick the best total. Looking at cost only ignores risk and fairness, which the club also decided matter.
a.clue: The decision uses all the criteria together.

b.q: Sam scores two phone plans from 1 to 5. Plan A: cost 5, risk 2, fairness 3. Plan B: cost 3, risk 4, fairness 4. Which does best overall, with all criteria equal?
opts: Plan B, with a total of 11
Plan A, with a total of 10
Plan A, because it has the best cost
Both plans, with equal totals
b.why: Plan A totals 5 + 2 + 3 = 10. Plan B totals 3 + 4 + 4 = 11. Plan A wins on cost, but with equal weights the best total decides.

a.best: The one with the highest total score

b.best: Plan B, with a total of 11

problems.detail: The stem gives 'risk 2' and 'risk 4' without saying that 5 is the best score. A student could read 'risk 4' as more risky, which is worse. It should say 'from 1 (poor) to 5 (very good)', as the card does.

check.summary: The card and both answers are correct. Question b should say that 5 is the best score, because 'risk 4' could be read as higher risk.
